Use case: stylized-concept. Project art bible for Grayhaven, a fictional 1985 Northern California fishing/logging town. Original narrative oil-painting realism influenced by the Peredvizhniki's observed everyday life and the expressive paint handling of Disco Elysium, without copying game assets. Believable architectural/object structure, bold mid-scale directional brushwork, broad connected value masses, selective lost edges, warm lived-in details amid cold coastal atmosphere. Palette: bone #E7DDC8, ink #24282B, umber #8A7968, ochre #B58A50, rust #984F43, mist #A8B3AE, teal #496669, olive #666D50, violet-grey #696373, amber #D9AE70. Not photorealistic, not watercolor or pastel, no plastic toy diorama, no global black outlines, no noise filter. No people, portraits, humanoids or characters. No invented story clues. All text only exact short English labels requested; no illegible annotation paragraphs. Landscape editorial concept-art board, high resolution, elegant ivory margins, dark serif headings, numbered panels. Footer 'DESIGN STUDY / NOT AN ENGINE CAPTURE'.
Title '01 / PAINTED REALITY'. Top half a richly painted elevated orthographic view of a humble wood-clad northern California diner corner, wet timber, window and cup: attention at entrance, background trees dissolve into broad brush masses. Bottom half four clearly separated studies labeled 'VALUE', 'BRUSH', 'EDGE', 'MATERIAL': grayscale massing sketch of same corner, directional oil brush swatches, same wood/window hard-soft-lost edge study, eight small material samples (painted wood, raw wood, plaster, stone, cloth, metal, glass, water). Include ten small swatches in specified palette without hex text. A restrained small comparison strip labeled 'AVOID': dense repeated grain, plastic glossy wall, uniform black outline. Main art should clearly exemplify mid-scale oil strokes rather than microtexture. Maintain airy grid.

Title '03 / BLUEBIRD — SPACE & STRUCTURE'. Three large equal panels across the upper two thirds: 'EXTERIOR', 'GROUND FLOOR', 'UPPER FLOOR'. Same building across panels and fixed elevated orthographic viewing direction. Exterior has a wide two-storey painted timber main block, stepped false storefront front, faded muted blue sign reading 'BLUEBIRD', a separate lower single-storey rear kitchen wing. Dining: front street glass door and side windows beside dark green booths, long maple lunch counter with fixed red stools, espresso machine and pastry cabinet, double swinging doors to rear kitchen, milk-glass pendant shades. Kitchen stainless workbench and black cast-iron stockpot on a gas stove; no exterior back door. Stairs connect kitchen to upper home. Upper home: small sitting room and bedroom, rocking chair at street-facing window, round white-clothed table, dresser, iron bed and shaded bedside lamp; no full second storey over kitchen. Show true cutaway with continuous solid floor, partial foreground wall, complete protected furniture, warm side-window light with cool shadows, no floating objects. Bottom third: separate monochrome isometric structural studies labeled 'SHELL', 'SHADOW', 'CONTENTS', then eight distinct material swatches. Shadow study shows hidden roof remains logical light blocker. Broad expressive oil surfaces, coherent geometry. Concept schematic only, not measured engineering drawing.

Title '04 / OBJECTS WITH A HISTORY'. Precise spacious 3 columns x 2 rows object production-study grid, each cell large hero three-quarter orthographic view plus two smaller simplified silhouette views of the SAME object (far, mid, near visual LOD). Exactly six objects: '01 ENAMEL MUG' ivory enamel steel mug with small chipped rim revealing dark steel and clean reflective inside; '02 STEW POT' heavy black open cast-iron fish-stew stockpot with two small loop handles, darkened underside, on neutral tabletop, no lid needed; '03 ROTARY PHONE' black 1980s desk rotary telephone with handset on cradle and coiled cord, worn handle; '04 BRASS KEY' ordinary old brass room key with plain tag, no number or symbol, smooth worn edges; '05 GEAR LOCKER' practical weathered grey wood dock cabinet on small feet, two closed doors, salt stains at base; '06 MOORING POST' stout vertical rough timber bollard with a deep rope-worn groove and frayed rope loop at lower neck. Neutral bone grey backing and grounded contact shadows. Tiny small flat pigment/material swatches next to each. No added keys/objects, no mysterious marks. Show actual medium oil strokes clearly. Objects remain mechanically credible with no melted geometry. Spatial framing each item fully visible. Do not turn UI into generated technical dimensions.

Title '05 / A LANDSCAPE TO READ'. Layout top 65 percent one large elevated fixed-direction orthographic town composition, NOT a parchment map: broad crescent bay and muted open sea west/left, long grey sandy coast, town clustered inland east/right around north-south main street, single straight timber pier at southern harbor, lighthouse farther south on separate headland, redwood hills enclosing north/east/south, sparse sawmill upper-right inland and isolated station on northern ridge. Sense of whole coastal landscape, no floating island, no ocean all around land, sea is large calm negative space. Do not label or invent routes; diagram is composition-only. Bottom 35 percent three equal tighter orthographic environment paintings: 'MAIN STREET' warm grey timber shop fronts and faded blue diner sign, 'COAST' weathered pier salt timber and grey sand, 'REDWOODS' colossal vertical trunks surrounding grounded clearing and fallen log. Strong compositional value grouping, much less microdetail in distant tree masses, expressive oil paint and lost edges in fog. No miniature toy architecture. Same palette and atmosphere all panels.

Title '06 / LIGHT ORGANISES SPACE'. Strict 4 columns x 2 rows editorial contact sheet. First six panels show EXACT SAME elevated orthographic diner street-corner composition, camera, geometry and objects, changing only light, divided row-major: '03:00 PREDAWN', '07:00 MORNING', '15:00 AFTERNOON', '18:30 SUNSET', '20:00 BLUE HOUR', '23:00 NIGHT'. Diner is two-storey timber main block with faded blue sign and low rear wing, a street door and windows, adjacent damp street and distant redwoods; lamp and window positions identical every panel. Night subtle cool ambient still readable with localized amber windows, morning pale ochre side light, afternoon neutral warm directional, sunset amber facing planes violet-grey shadows, blue hour cool sky restrained warm windows. Last two panels 'INTERIOR / DAY', 'INTERIOR / NIGHT': exactly same roof-removed orthographic dining room with solid floor, green booth seats, long maple counter, red stools, back swinging door, two rows milk-glass hanging lamps. Day window-side illumination, night warm ceiling fixtures and cool unlit recesses. No floodlit night, no black crushed details, no bloom haze, no geometry differences. Maintain expressive directional oil brush surfaces. Explicitly a painted lighting intention sheet.
